articles.title: Gulf exports more oil than it did before Iran war despite surge in Hormuz attacks
articles.summary:
Gulf exports more oil than it did before Iran war despite surge in Hormuz attacks

The Middle East is now exporting more oil than it did before the US-Israeli war on Iran began on 28 February, posing a challenge to the Islamic Republic as it looks to cement its control over the Strait of Hormuz and as the US and Israel threaten a new attack.

Gulf countries exported 24.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in the week ending 18 October, surpassing prewar levels of 23.3 million bpd, according to data released by energy analytics firm Kpler.

The surge in exports comes at a time when Iran's attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz have also surged.

At least 12 attacks took place last week, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO).

Read more: Gulf exports more oil than it did before Iran war despite surge in Hormuz attacks

Israeli forces killed a man with disabilities on Thursday during an incursion in a village in Syria's Daraa governorate, state media reported.

The killing follows reports of Israeli forces storming into the village, where they searched several properties, deployed snipers on the rooftops of civilian homes and fired "indiscriminately" across residential neighbourhoods.

Vance says he is 'not endorsing' Netanyahu in Israeli election

US Vice President JD Vance told reporters that he is "not endorsing" Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu just days before Israeli parliamentary elections are set to take place. 

"I’m not attacking Bibi Netanyahu. I’m not endorsing Bibi Netanyahu," he said during a press conference in Ohio ahead of Israel's election on 27 October.

Vance said that he was instead focused on the 3 November US midterm elections, adding that he would not back any more foreign candidates, following his previous backing of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban that
didn’t go particularly well".

articles.title: Iran calls on UN to slam 'unlawful threats' from US, Israel
articles.summary:
Iran calls on UN to slam 'unlawful threats' from US, Israel

Iran’s envoy to the United Nations, Gholamhossein Darzi, has urged the UN secretary-general and the president of the Security Council to reject and denounce the US and Israel for their repeated "threats" against Tehran.

In a letter addressed to the UN, Darzi said that Tehran has the right to self-defence as a response to any act of aggression. 

He also warned of "continuous threats" from the US and Israel, including the possible usage of the "Mother of All Bombs" - known officially as the Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) - against Iran. 

"Threatening to use the 'MOAB' bomb (the Mother of All Bombs) against Iran's civilian infrastructure and to target all of the country's energy infrastructure constitutes, among other things, a flagrant violation of international law," he added.

Iran called on the the security council to demand Washington and Tel Aviv put an end to their "unlawful threats", as well as ensure accountability and reparations for damage from "wrongful acts committed by the United States and the Israeli regime against Iran".
